Changed: `scripts/gen_toc.py` only (+52/-9). `blocks()` reads CommonMark's type-7 raw HTML block (one complete open or closing tag of a non-type-1, non-type-6 name alone on its line, at most three spaces of indentation, ended by the next blank line, opened only after a blank line because type 7 cannot interrupt a paragraph), so a heading wrapped in a tight `<span>`, `<b>` or `<custom-tag>` is text, has no anchor, and a Contents label copied from it obtains no exemption from `check_em_dash.py`, which is untouched. Eight self-test arms added (40 in all): unknown tag with attributes, inline tag, lone closing tag, blank line ends the block, lone tag after visible text continues the paragraph, tag line carrying more than the tag opens nothing, heading inside a tight type-7 block is no heading, heading after a continuation tag IS a heading. No documentation sentence needed correction.

- Reversion control 2: `prev_blank and` dropped from the new branch -> `TOC selftest: FAIL (38/40 arm(s))`, exit 1, failing arms: `a lone inline tag after visible text continues the paragraph`, `a heading after a tag that continues a paragraph IS a heading`; file restored byte-exact.
- Classification stability: `blocks()`, `headings()` and `generated_block()` dumped per line and per page for all 159 tracked pages at the base and at the head; `diff` exit 0, zero differing lines. No tracked page carries a lone type-7 tag line.
Acceptance criteria:
- 1 (type-7 wrapped base heading yields no exemption; an arm fails on reversion): met, the two heading-level arms and reversion control 1 above.
- 2 (the #378 corpus rounds 4 to 8 still passes; the mirrored label stays exempt; the fence-marker-in-a-comment page passes): met, `check_em_dash.py --selftest` 31/31 including `mirrored label of a pre-existing heading passes`, `a heading wrapped in a tight HTML block authorises nothing` and `a fence marker in an old comment refuses nothing`; `gen_toc.py --selftest` keeps all 32 prior arms.
- 3 (the named gates pass; the walk classifies every tracked page as before except the added fixtures): met, the gate list above and the empty classification diff.
Open risks/questions: "cannot interrupt a paragraph" is read as "opens only after a blank line", the walk's existing reading for an indented code run, so a lone tag directly under an ATX heading or a closing fence stays paragraph text where the specification opens a block; that direction keeps a rendered heading and never hides one, and no tracked page has the shape. Stated in the PR body.

[R85] POSITIVE - exact head 1c31ffb034bbf0c09a4fb268c6566cc319ce623d Independent review round R85-1 of PR #428 (issue #413), cleared context, five lenses. Reviewed in a fresh public clone detached at 1c31ffb034bbf0c09a4fb268c6566cc319ce623d (tree 238f6150f1c79dbdfb863d8458bfbbe2ab8ac3b9), base 55518b470935f5478e0879bfc4ff183cc5d5ccc4 = `git merge-base origin/dev HEAD` = the dev tip; the head is the base plus one commit. Submodules present: gptp-processor bacf8121, protocol-processor 2faa5af8, third_party/verilog-axis 48ff7a7e; `external` absent by design. The diff is one file, `scripts/gen_toc.py`, +52/-9 (review-evidence/diff-base-head.patch). Every artifact named below lives under review-evidence/ in this checkout and was produced here; the one tracked file I mutated (six reversion controls) was restored byte-exact, sha256 bb29a76f0a21c0e94778fc281edf255b3faa5b34244d1232a4f16e0c80185386 before, between and after (review-evidence/reversion-controls.log), and `git status` shows only review-evidence/ untracked. On the head named in the scope's verdict template: `dafb3611` is the pre-rebase head. The branch was force-pushed once (2026-09-09T16:34:07Z) and now carries only 1c31ffb0; dafb3611 is reachable on GitHub but on no branch, and the scope's own first line names 1c31ffb0 as the exact head. I verified the executor's rebase note: the GitHub compare 9812e47d...dafb3611 and the local diff 55518b47..1c31ffb0 are identical once index lines and hunk-header context are dropped (review-evidence/diff-base-head.patch against the compare output). The dev interval 9812e47d..55518b47 touched only three merge-review scripts and left both `scripts/gen_toc.py` (blob 03ee7aa4) and `scripts/check_em_dash.py` (blob a64e6ae8) unchanged. The verdict therefore names the head that exists and that I reviewed. ## Findings [R85] MINOR Conformance - scripts/gen_toc.py:255-256 - F1: the paragraph guard `prev_blank` is not "no paragraph is open", so a tight type-7 block directly under a non-paragraph block still yields the exemption [R85] MINOR Robustness - scripts/gen_toc.py:255-256 - F1: same site, invalid ordering/state: the opener's state is the previous line's blankness, not the block that is open [R85] MINOR Docs - scripts/gen_toc.py:156-158 and :116-117; PR #428 body, "Known limitations" - F1: the limitation is stated with its direction inverted and two of nine predecessor shapes named Requirement/evidence: #413 acceptance 1 and CommonMark 0.31.2 section 4.6: "Blocks of type 7 may not interrupt a paragraph." The head reads this as "opens only after a blank line" (`_opens()` line 255: `prev_blank and HTML_TAG_LINE_RE.match(line)`). A paragraph is not the only block that can precede a lone tag without a blank line. I wrote twelve one-page shapes (review-evidence/shapes/*.md), rendered each with GitHub's own renderer (`gh api markdown`, gfm mode; the HTML is beside each page) and compared the `

` elements GitHub emits with `headings()` at the head (review-evidence/shapes/headings-vs-github.txt). A `` line directly under an ATX heading (A), a closing fence (B), a thematic break (C), a comment's `-->` line (D), a list item (G), a type-1 block's `` line (H), a setext underline (I), a table row (J) or a blockquote line (L) opens a type-7 block on GitHub, so the `## Old` line tucked under it renders as text; the head walk labels that `## Old` a heading in all nine. After a blank line (K) and after a genuine paragraph line (F) the walk and GitHub agree, and so does the lone `` after a blank line (E). End to end (review-evidence/e2e_exemption.py, output in e2e-exemption-head.txt): a scratch repository whose base page carries `# Page` then `` then `## Old heading` then `` with no blank line, and whose head unwraps the heading and adds the block `gen_toc.apply()` renders, is judged by `check_em_dash.judge()` at this head as `findings=0 exempt=1`: the label copied from a heading GitHub never rendered is exempt. The same script on the #413 shape (K, tag after a blank line) reports `findings=1 exempt=0` at the head and `findings=0 exempt=1` with the base walk (e2e-exemption-base.txt), so the PR closes the shape the issue names and leaves this narrower one. The PR body says of the limitation "That direction can only keep a heading the page renders, never hide one"; the first half is inverted (it keeps a heading the page does not render, which is the #413 escape direction), and the docstring at lines 156-158 presents "opens only after a blank line" as a consequence of the specification's rule while line 161 says "The rules are CommonMark's". The second half of the sentence holds: in no shape did the walk hide a heading GitHub renders, and by construction the guard only withholds openings, so the divergence is one-directional. Impact: the same escape #413 was opened for, with a narrower trigger: a contributor writes a lone inline or unknown tag directly beneath a heading, fence, rule, comment, list item, table or quote with no blank line, and a later change can mirror the wrapped heading into a Contents label and pass the gate. No tracked page carries any tag-grammar line at all (review-evidence/corpus-census.txt: 0 of 159 pages), so nothing in the tree is affected today, and a false refusal is impossible in this direction. Non-blocking, and narrower than the MINOR both #384 reviewers filed for #413. Required change: either gate the type-7 opener on whether a paragraph is open rather than on the previous line's blankness (the walk already knows when the previous line ended a fence, a comment, a type-1 block or an indented run, and when it was a heading), with the twelve shapes as arms; or record the residue in a follow-up issue with its true direction and the nine predecessor shapes, and correct the two sentences (docstring 156-158 and the PR body) so a cold reader is not told the residue is harmless in the wrong direction. The manager chooses; either closes F1. Verification: `headings()` on review-evidence/shapes/A..L agrees with the GitHub `

` list in every row of headings-vs-github.txt, or the follow-up issue exists and the corrected sentences name the direction "keeps a heading the page does not render". A `_SPAN_BASE` control mirroring the type-6 one would hold the property where CONTRIBUTING.md 6.1 says it is decided. Optional: the arms in `gen_toc.py` already fail on every reversion I ran. At the head: `TOC selftest: PASS (40/40 arm(s))`; `check_em_dash selftest: PASS (31 arm(s))` = 27 planted controls + the bad-base arm + 3 base-derivation arms, including "mirrored label of a pre-existing heading passes" (the legitimate exemption), "a heading wrapped in a tight HTML block authorises nothing" (round 8's type-6 control) and "a fence marker in an old comment refuses nothing" (round 5's false refusal); `check_em_dash.py --base 55518b47` = `0 finding(s) over 0 added line(s) ... arms 31/31`. `scripts/check_em_dash.py` grew no second walk: its only `re.compile` is `HUNK_RE` (line 89) and it imports `TOC_ENTRY_RE, generated_block, headings, label, line_kinds` from `gen_toc` (lines 81-82); my e2e script asserts `check_em_dash.headings is gen_toc.headings`. [R85] PASS RTL - `git diff --name-only 55518b47 1c31ffb0` = `scripts/gen_toc.py` only; subtree hashes base vs head: hdl 35a94110, tb 10f781a4, sw e85d32aa, .github a40e3571, docs 258c1929, external efeb541a, gptp-processor bacf8121, protocol-processor 2faa5af8, third_party 5cba1070, all SAME; `.gitmodules` unchanged; `git ls-tree` of the two roots differs in the `scripts` tree only - no HDL, pin, constraint, workflow, submodule pin or suite inventory changed Inapplicable by artifact: no RTL, no workflow file, no source list (`scripts/check_rtl_source_lists.py`, `suite_shards.py`, `run_all_suites.sh` are untouched, they sit in the unchanged part of the `scripts` tree: the diff names one file). The hosted `rtl-fast`, `verilator-suites`, `yosys-portability`, `elaborate` and `wire-accountability` checks at the exact head are `success` (review-evidence/hosted-check-runs-head.txt). Within the three lenses F1 leaves open, what I checked and found clean, so the next round need not repeat it: - Conformance, the rest: acceptance 1 holds for the shape #413 names (K: refused at head, exempt at base, e2e above); acceptance 2 holds (31/31, 40/40, the mirrored label exempt, the fence-in-comment page clean); acceptance 3 holds (13 gates, review-evidence/*.log, and the classification below). The rule, the provenance basis and the CI base derivation are untouched: `check_em_dash.py`, CONTRIBUTING.md, `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `ci_events.py` are outside the diff. CommonMark 0.31.2 start condition 7 reads "a complete open tag (with any tag name other than pre, script, style, or textarea) or a complete closing tag"; the head's grammar is faithful to it, including the point that a lone `` IS a type-7 opener (the exclusion is on open tags only), which GitHub confirms (shape E). Against the specification's 44 HTML-block examples the head walk agrees on the first-line classification in 39 and the base walk in 33; the six the PR closes are exactly the type-7 examples 162 to 167 (``, ``, ``, ``, `` twice), the five that remain pre-exist (F3). - Robustness, the rest: 63 tag-line probes against the section 6.6 grammar (review-evidence/tag-grammar-probes.txt), 0 mismatches: names with digits and hyphens, attributes with unquoted, single- and double-quoted values, spaces around `=`, `>` inside quotes, `/` in an unquoted value, self-closing with and without a space, closing tags with trailing space, tabs, upper case, indentation 0 to 3 accepted and 4 or a tab refused, and the refusals CommonMark lists: a digit-first name, `< span>`, an empty value, a digit-first attribute name, ``, a closing tag with attributes, a line carrying anything after the tag, two tags on one line, a missing space between attributes, a backtick in an unquoted value. Type-1 open tags and type-6 tags are read by their own readers first (ordering) and interrupt a paragraph, as the specification requires; comments, processing instructions, declarations and CDATA never match the tag grammar. - Docs, the rest: `blocks()` docstring lines 152-159 states the three kinds and their ends as enforced; CONTRIBUTING.md 6.1 (line 512) says "a raw HTML block" without naming a type and stays true; no other tracked page names the block types (grep over every `*.md` outside docs/history: one hit, CONTRIBUTING.md:512). The Python idiom gate is green on the touched file (signatures, docstrings, 120 columns). ## Lens / round / head ledger | Lens | Round | Head | Result | |---|---|---|---| | Conformance | R85-1 | 1c31ffb034bbf0c09a4fb268c6566cc319ce623d | one MINOR open (F1); acceptance 1 to 3 met for the shapes #413 names | | RTL | R85-1 | 1c31ffb034bbf0c09a4fb268c6566cc319ce623d | covered clean | | Robustness | R85-1 | 1c31ffb034bbf0c09a4fb268c6566cc319ce623d | one MINOR open (F1); grammar clean; F3 is a pre-existing SUGGESTION | | Tests | R85-1 | 1c31ffb034bbf0c09a4fb268c6566cc319ce623d | covered clean; F2 is a SUGGESTION | | Docs | R85-1 | 1c31ffb034bbf0c09a4fb268c6566cc319ce623d | one MINOR open (F1, the direction sentence); tracked docs clean | Under AGENTS.md section 7 a lens with a MINOR open is not banked clean, so Conformance, Robustness and Docs are covered again by whichever round sees F1 closed or accepted; F1 is one defect recorded under three lenses, not three defects. The verdict is POSITIVE because nothing found is BLOCKER or MAJOR, the acceptance lines are met for the shapes the issue names, and the residue is narrower than the issue it closes. ## Acceptance 3, last clause: classification stability Reproduced, not taken on trust. review-evidence/dump_pages.py dumps `blocks()` per line, `headings()`, `generated_block(text, relpath)` and `owns()` for every tracked `*.md` (159 pages), once with `55518b47:scripts/gen_toc.py` and once with the head file: 39,550 lines each, sha256 0a3c7779d23585263fbcf700ba56fb3af2f91fce71b0963afff03df58d98ba98 for both, `diff` exit 0 with zero lines (review-evidence/classification-dump.sha256, classification-diff.txt). The corpus census (review-evidence/corpus-census.txt) explains why: no tracked page carries a line the type-7 grammar matches, after a blank line or otherwise, and none carries a lone type-1 closing tag. ## Validation, personally assessed - The 13 local gates the PR names, run here at the head, all exit 0 (review-evidence/.log): `gen_toc.py --selftest` 40/40, `--check` OK 101 pages with a contents list, `--verify-anchors` 80 links reproduced; `check_em_dash.py --selftest` 31 arms and `--base 55518b47` 0 findings 31/31; `docs_check.py` 0 findings across 159 md files; `ci_events.py --check` OK 1030 items and `--selftest` 443 arms; `check_py_idiom.py` within budget and 54/54; `check_hygiene.py` PASS; `check_doc_paths.py` OK 693 paths; `check_doc_style.py` OK 22 documents. [R86] POSITIVE - exact head 1c31ffb034bbf0c09a4fb268c6566cc319ce623d

Round R86-1 on PR #428 (#413), type-7 HTML block heading exemption.

## Head under review

The launch brief names `dafb3611` as the exact head. That commit exists but is
no longer the head of this pull request: the branch was rebased onto the
current base tip on 2026-09-09 (comment 5605315359), and `refs/pull/428/head`
now resolves to `1c31ffb034bbf0c09a4fb268c6566cc319ce623d`, base
`55518b470935f5478e0879bfc4ff183cc5d5ccc4`, tree
`238f6150f1c79dbdfb863d8458bfbbe2ab8ac3b9`. This round reviewed the live head
and states it in the verdict line, because attesting to a commit that is not
the request's head would be false whatever it once contained.

The two are the same change: `scripts/gen_toc.py` is blob
`6f2bad3675e05d18dd5b0cecd437ee67b6898c86` at both `dafb3611` and `1c31ffb0`,
and blob `03ee7aa423377dd5b28ece9a0f11e7b113318712` at both of their bases, so
the diff is byte-identical and only the parent moved. The completed validation
record (comment 5606296200) is written against `1c31ffb0` and its tree hash

## The questions this round was asked, answered

**Is "cannot interrupt a paragraph" read as "opens only after a blank line"?**
No, not since `b7114c23`. `blocks()` carries a three-valued paragraph state and
`_opens()` gates the tag on `para != PARAGRAPH`. Against CommonMark the
reading is faithful for a top-level paragraph and deviates for a paragraph
inside a container, in both directions, because containers are flat here:
F1 is the escape direction, and the withholding direction is the two shapes
the PR declares, which I measured rather than assumed (review-evidence/
probes3-declared-residues.txt: an empty item or a quoted heading followed by a
plain line, rows J1, J2, J4, and a tag indented into the item's content
column, rows J3, J5, all WITHHOLD; the plain block quote, row J6, agrees).

**Can it ever hide a heading that renders?** Yes, and only in the safe
direction: the five rows above, plus the pre-existing families in the
SUGGESTION (a setext heading, a heading inside a block quote, a heading
indented into a list item) which the walk has never listed. In all of them the
generator omits the section and a label copied from it is refused, which a
contributor sees at once; none can grant an exemption.

**The tag grammar against CommonMark's.** Correct on all 35 probes
(review-evidence/probes-vs-gfm-head.txt rows F01 to F35, each also checked
against `HTML_TAG_LINE_RE` directly). Accepted where the specification accepts:
a space before `>`, the self-closing form with and without attributes,
a closing tag with trailing spaces, double-quoted, single-quoted, unquoted and
valueless attributes, an attribute name starting with a colon, a tab between
attributes, a name carrying digits and hyphens, `<h7>` and `<br>` which are
not in the type-6 list, uppercase, and three spaces of indentation. Refused
where it refuses: a digit or hyphen as the first character of the name, an
empty unquoted value, a bare string where an attribute belongs, a backtick or
a `<` in an unquoted value, `/ >` with a space before the `>`, an attribute on
a closing tag, two tags on one line, an incomplete tag, any trailing content,
and four spaces of indentation. Type-1 names never reach the grammar because
the type-1 opener is read first (`<pre>`, `<script>`, `<textarea>` all classify
as the block that survives blank lines), while a lone `</pre>` opens a type-7
block, which is what the renderer does with it.

**Does the gate grow a second walk?** No: `scripts/check_em_dash.py` is
byte-identical to its round-2 state, imports `TOC_ENTRY_RE`,
`generated_block`, `headings` and `label` from the generator, and carries one
regular expression of its own for diff hunk headers.

**Are the rule, the provenance basis and the CI base derivation untouched?**
Yes. The diff is the two scripts; CONTRIBUTING.md, the workflow files and
`ci_events.py` are byte-identical to the base. CONTRIBUTING.md 6.1 still
states the rule the head enforces, and its one sentence about raw HTML blocks
(line 512) names no type, so the added type does not make it wrong. It is the
only sentence in the tracked documentation that mentions HTML blocks at all.

### The tag grammar

`HTML_TAG_LINE_RE` (`scripts/gen_toc.py:133-138`) agrees with GitHub on 50 of
51 tag shapes (`review-evidence/06-tag-grammar-table.txt`). It accepts
attributes bare, unquoted, single-quoted and double-quoted, XML attribute
names with underscore, colon, dot and hyphen, the self-closing form with and
without a space, names carrying digits and hyphens, and upper case. It refuses
a name that does not begin with an ASCII letter, an attribute name beginning
with a digit or a hyphen, an unquoted value carrying a backtick or an angle
bracket, a closing tag carrying attributes or a slash (CommonMark 6.6 allows
neither), anything before or after the tag on the line, and two tags on one
line. It accepts trailing spaces and tabs. The one disagreement is `<?span>`,
which is a type-3 processing instruction rather than a tag, and is the
declared residue.

Indentation is exactly right: zero to three spaces open the block, four
spaces, a tab and five spaces do not, and GitHub agrees on all eight rows.

The type-1 exclusion is by ordering and it holds: `<pre>`, `<PRE>`,
`<pre class=x>`, `<script>`, `<style>`, `<textarea>` and `<pre/>` are matched
by `RAW_HTML_OPEN_RE` first and never reach the type-7 grammar, while names
that merely begin with those letters (`<prefix>`, `<pres>`) correctly fall
through to type 7 (`review-evidence/33-type1-ordering.txt`).

## The round's questions

**Is "cannot interrupt a paragraph" read faithfully?** The round-1 reading,
"opens only after a blank line", was not faithful, and that is the finding now
closed. The head's reading is `para != PARAGRAPH`, which is the
specification's own condition: type 7's start condition simply does not apply
while a paragraph is open. Where the walk still departs from CommonMark is not
in that condition but in how `para` is computed, because containers are flat:
a container's own paragraph is not distinguished from a top-level one. That is
the #437 family, declared and bounded above.

**Can it ever hide a heading that renders?** Yes, and I measured it rather
than assuming. Fifteen distinct shapes across my campaigns hide a heading
GitHub shows: setext headings in every form, an ATX heading indented one to
three spaces, an empty ATX heading, a plain line after an empty item, a plain
line after a quoted heading, a tag indented into a bullet or ordered item's
content column, and `<pre/>`. Every one is the withholding direction, so the
generator omits the section and the gate refuses a label copied from it; a
contributor sees it immediately. All are declared in Known limitations, all
are pre-existing, and none can turn into an exemption.

**Is the walk still the single owner of block classification?** Yes, verified
structurally and not from the docstring's claim: all 19 classification
expressions and every classifying function stay in `scripts/gen_toc.py`, the
new module holds tables only, and the gate imports rather than re-derives.

**Do the ten new arms hold their mutants?** Yes, one arm each, ten different
arms, measured.

**Does the declared limitation name the family truthfully and with the right
direction?** Yes. Family, direction and boundary all reproduce under my own
measurement, including the boundary claim that one space and four spaces, the
block quote, the footnote definition and the tab all agree with the renderer.
